name: Wyoming
summary_text: Travel documents are the sharpest exposure for a trans visitor to Wyoming, because Wyoming stands under the United States federal framework. Executive Order 14168, signed 20 January 2025, redefined sex for federal purposes as a male-female binary, barred transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with their gender identity, prohibited self-selection of gender on passports and visas, and directed the attorney general to correct the misapplication of Bostock v. Clayton County (2020). The State Department stopped processing the X marker and any marker not matching sex assigned at birth; new passport applications are processed only as M or F according to supporting documents, and passports already issued with an X remain valid until they expire. In November 2025 the Supreme Court allowed the passport sex-marker restrictions to take effect, superseding a State Department policy in place since 1992. Trans and nonbinary travellers report passports confiscated or blocked at application, with some left stranded abroad; the ACLU has sued the State Department on behalf of seven plaintiffs, and Lambda Legal maintains guidance on how name and gender changes interact with federal records.  Facilities access inside Wyoming is restricted by statute. On Monday, 3 March 2025, Governor Mark Gordon signed two measures into law. House Bill 72, the Protecting Privacy in Public Spaces Act, covers sex-designated restrooms, showers, sleeping quarters and locker rooms at public facilities. Senate File 62, Sex-Designated Facilities and Public Schools, requires public school children from pre-kindergarten upward, including charter school students, to use restrooms aligned with sex assigned at birth; districts must provide a reasonable accommodation to any student who does not wish to use a multiple-occupancy restroom or locker room matching the gender at that student's birth. The Movement Advancement Project equality map records these Wyoming facility bans alongside the year of enactment.  A national legal-risk assessment published in July 2026 lists Wyoming among the worst states for legislation targeting transgender adults. The assessment draws on five years of daily legislative tracking and a rubric identifying the most severe bills, and it was republished on 27 August 2026 by a regional LGBTQ outlet. The same assessment records federal policies that continue to generate legal difficulty for transgender people across the country.

name: Aruba
summary_text: Aruba stands under the national framework of the Netherlands and applies its own Criminal Code (Wetboek van Strafrecht / Kódigo Penal), enacted in 2012. The Code prohibits unfair discrimination and incitement to hatred and violence on grounds including heterosexual or homosexual orientation. Article 1:221 defines discrimination as any distinction, exclusion, restriction or preference that has the purpose or effect of affecting recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental liberties in political, economic, social, cultural or other areas of social life. Articles 2:61 and 2:62 punish such discrimination and incitement with fines and imprisonment up to one year. Gender identity and gender expression are not addressed in the enumerated grounds.  Same-sex sexual activity is legal in Aruba for both male and female conduct. The age of consent is 16 and is equal for heterosexual and homosexual intercourse.  Same-sex marriage has been legal since the 12 July 2024 ruling of the Supreme Court of the Netherlands, which upheld the Appeals Court decision barring discrimination based on sexual orientation. A prior ruling of 13 April 2007 by the Dutch Supreme Court had required Aruba to recognize same-sex marriages registered in the Netherlands and in Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba, after the Aruban government refused recognition to a lesbian couple married in the Netherlands.  Registered partnerships open to both same-sex and opposite-sex couples have been available since the parliamentary vote of 8 September 2016 extending civil-code marriage articles to registered same-sex unions. The regime confers spousal pension rights and emergency medical decision rights. Marriages performed in the Netherlands were already recognized kingdom-wide before that vote.  Commercial provision for LGBT visitors is widespread. Venues, hotels and restaurants cater to or advertise as LGBT-friendly across the island, with several specific gay bars and clubs concentrated as an example in the capital city of Oranjestad. No documented statement about societal tolerance of transgender people specifically was provided, and no transgender-specific facts on facilities, screening, custody, care or protection were provided.
